cars.specification_market: Original Monteverdi High Speed production-road family, selected 375 L 2+2 standard 7.2-litre engine and 1974 range updates described in Automobil Revue issue 45 of 1973. Eleven attributes map to that original single-page period report. The 305 DIN-PS at 4500 rpm figure is explicitly tied to reported German TUV approval after emissions changes; do not equate it with earlier 375 SAE hp, a generic net rating, the optional 390-PS 7-litre Hemi or modern feature factfile. Rounded 7.2 litres remains rounded. The 8-litre enlarged oil sump is not total engine-oil capacity; the 4-litre expansion vessel is not total coolant capacity. Article covers both coupe and saloon: only stated shared updates and coupe-compatible transmission are used; no long-wheelbase saloon dimensions or seating transferred. Representative licensed Fissore 375L photo does not authenticate model year, later exterior trim or reference engine. Group High Speed S/L/C/4, body revisions and road engine options once conservatively. Dedicated racers, Hai prototypes, replicas and further body examples are not additional admissions.
cars.summary: The Monteverdi High Speed is a defining Swiss sporting grand-tourer programme, combining European coachwork and chassis development with Chrysler V8 power. Contemporary reporting and a later firsthand drive establish its continuing place among ambitious post-war GTs. Count the High Speed production-road family once across bodies, engines and years; rarity, price and cosmetic differences alone do not earn admission.

sources.notes: Custodian catalogue and original JPEG facsimile https://sammlung.verkehrshaus.ch/multimedia/6/multimedia-143316.large.jpg read. Original single page individually viewed; enlarged reading panels used for the Modelle 1974, engine/cooling, comfort and brief-drive sections. All eleven attributes map to its standard 7.2-litre 375 L 2+2 / 375/4 updates, selecting the coupe only. Output explicitly quoted as 305 DIN-PS at 4500 rpm after German TUV approval; no conversion or universal gross/net rating assumed. Optional 7-litre 390-PS Hemi and Hai test are separate. Sump volume is not total oil-system capacity. Brief coupe/saloon driving impressions are not a timed performance test. No maximum speed, acceleration, exact displacement, mass, dimensions, torque conversion or price imported.

sources.title: Monteverdi 375L: taking on the greats, 22 October 2025
sources.source_type: Original firsthand driving feature; family significance only
sources.notes: Full relevant historical, driving and factfile sections read. Firsthand short drive of a restored 1971-registered right-hand-drive Australian-delivery 375L supplies enduring GT context, not selected 1974 specifications. Period Autocar results are quoted secondhand there, not new measurements; originals were not read. The caption calls 375 net output while narrative distinguishes SAE rating from lower net output: no number transferred. No rarity totals, Ferrari-dispute anecdote, restoration claim or generalized 375-bhp/torque/dimension/weight figures applied to the selected emission-controlled reference.
